definitions.explanation: The first star visible in the evening sky, typically Venus when it appears as the evening star.

examples.japanese: {一番星|いちばんぼし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えた→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: I saw the first star (of the evening).

examples.japanese: {一番星|いちばんぼし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}い→願い：03529_negai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
examples.english: I make a wish upon the first star.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{暮|く}れて{一番星|いちばんぼし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{輝|かがや}き→輝く：02032_kagayaku⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: The sun set and the first star began to shine.

notes:
{一番星|いちばんぼし} is a poetic term for the first star visible at dusk.

ASTRONOMY:
The {一番星|いちばんぼし} is usually ⟦{金星|きんせい}→金星：15896_kinsei⟧ (Venus) when it appears as the ⟦{宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}→宵の明星：20968_yoinomyoujou⟧ (evening star).

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese folklore, making a wish upon the first star is similar to the Western "wish upon a star" tradition. The phrase 「{一番星|いちばんぼし}⟦{見|み}つけた→見つける：01180_mitsukeru⟧」 (I found the first star) is often said by children excited to spot it.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{宵|よい}の{明星|みょうじょう}→宵の明星：20968_yoinomyoujou⟧: evening star (Venus)
- ⟦{明|あ}け→明け：13157_ake⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{明星|みょうじょう}: morning star (Venus)
